title: Month shifts gave no clear UTC weekend rate difference in global M5.5+ earthquakes in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested the UTC weekend rate in 12,848 global ComCat earthquakes with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 in 2000-2025. The weekend to weekday rate ratio was 1.0151. The conditional 95% year resampling interval was 0.9619 to 1.0727. Circular shifts of daily counts within each calendar month gave a two-sided p value of 0.64595. Under this shift model, the standard deviation of weekend counts was 79.45% larger than under an independent-event model. Depth, magnitude, half-period and year-shift checks gave no clear difference. This is a catalog timing test, not evidence for equal physical rates or a cause. UTC pooling, a revised mixed-network catalog, event groups that cross block limits, and only 26 years limit the test. Code, source hashes, aggregate counts, simulation draws, a figure and an arithmetic audit are included. External event records stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Recorded UTC weekday rates and conditional 95% year resampling intervals for weekend to weekday rate ratios. Every interval includes one. Primary and year_shifts use the same events; small interval differences come from simulation seeds.
